title: Normalized presentation data for successive derived scalar extensions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For each sheaf $R$ of commutative rings write $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ for its module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $D(R)$ for their unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $a:R\to S$, let $U_a:\operatorname{Mod}(S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ be ordinary restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], let $E_a(M)=S\otimes_R M$ be sheafified scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and write $K(R)$ for the homotopy category with localization $Q_R:K(R)\to D(R)$.

A presentation $p_a$ consists of an additive ordinary functor with its object and morphism identifications with $E_a$, a functor $L_a:D(R)\to D(S)$, and a counit $\epsilon_a:L_aQ_R\to Q_SK(E_a)$ having the universal left-derived property. A section tensor $s\otimes x$ in the presented ordinary extension is the sheafification image of the ordinary pure tensor, transported by the object identification.

For a family $p=(p_a)_a$, a normalization is the following data and equations. It has ordinary and derived natural isomorphisms $E_bE_a\cong E_{ba}$ and $L_bL_a\cong L_{ba}$ for all composable ring maps $a:R\to S$, $b:S\to T$. The ordinary comparison sends $t\otimes(s\otimes x)$ to $b(s)t\otimes x$, and its inverse sends $t\otimes x$ to $t\otimes(1\otimes x)$. The derived comparison is represented by this ordinary comparison through the universal counits on every flat-term K-flat complex [def-pc-kflat-complex] [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The counits for $a$ and for the extension by $b$ of such a complex are invertible. It has ordinary adjunctions $E_a\dashv U_a$ with units $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, derived restrictions $V_a$ with factorizations $V_aQ_S\cong Q_RK(U_a)$, and adjunctions $L_a\dashv V_a$ whose units on those representatives agree, through the counits and factorization, with the localized ordinary units. It has ordinary restriction-composition isomorphisms $U_aU_b\cong U_{ba}$ equal to the identity on sections and derived restriction-composition isomorphisms $V_aV_b\cong V_{ba}$ equal to their localizations through the factorization isomorphisms. The composite derived extension unit equals the direct unit under these comparisons. For three successive extensions the two composites of the derived comparison agree, with the equality transport for associativity of ring-map composition. Finally, for a commuting diagram of two composable ring maps, coefficient-square comparison is the first derived composition comparison, transport by the commuting-square equality, and the inverse of the second derived composition comparison; pasting two such squares agrees with the outer square under the composition comparisons.

These are data types, not assertions that such data exist. They are the existing $\mathrm{Modules}$, restriction, pure section, Presentation, sectionTensor, squareComparison and Normalization declarations. No presentation, normalization, tensor functor or adjunction is selected by this definition.
